issues.failure_explanation: Reduced DoFs are fixed by F_i(v)=F_i(Pi_m^K v), where Pi_m^K is the L^2 projection on the 3D element K. In the edge serendipity space the reduced DoFs include tangential face moments [2] of order beta_d+1..beta_d'. These are unavoidable because computing Pi_l needs beta_d' large. In the node space, reduced DoFs include edge and face moments. Two elements sharing a face F have different projections Pi_m^{K1}v and Pi_m^{K2}v, so their reduced face/edge moments differ. The tangential (resp. scalar) trace on F is therefore not single-valued. The paper asserts that boundary continuity and conformity are preserved, but nothing establishes it, and the construction contradicts it.

issues.why_classification: Conformity is a headline property. Restoring it requires redesigning how boundary DoFs are reduced, which is new construction and analysis, and the edge case cannot simply avoid reducing face DoFs.

issues.failure_explanation: S-identifiability only says that preserved DoFs are unisolvent on S. It does not make (v,p), for p in S, a function of the preserved DoFs of v in V. Example (face space): P^3_m = grad P_{m+1} + x times P^3_{m-1}, and the moments (v, x times p) with deg p > k_r are reduced DoFs [3]. Whenever k_r < m-1, which the definition allows, Pi_m v depends on reduced DoFs. Similarly, the node space only gives Pi_{k_v} with k_v unrestricted. Consequences: (i) eqdefvs becomes an implicit fixed-point condition whose solvability and unisolvence (dim V^S = N_S) are unproved; (ii) Pi^S is not computable from the serendipity DoFs; (iii) the identity F_i(I^S v)=F_i(Pi_m I v) used in every interpolation proof needs Pi_m(I^S v - I v)=0, which is exactly this claim. The Gram-matrix variant in the Remark is circular, since the Lagrange basis of V^S presupposes V^S.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the preserved DoFs determine (v,p)_K for all p in S, and verify it per space. This means keeping face [3] up to m-1, edge [2],[4] up to m and [5] up to m-1, and node interior moments up to m. issues.why_classification: A verifiable hypothesis restricting which DoFs may be reduced restores the construction and the rates. It limits the serendipity reduction but leaves a recognizably comparable method.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof gives only the integration-by-parts identities that yield commuting diagrams for the standard interpolants. It never treats reduced DoFs. For u = I^{Se}v, the edge constraint on reduced [4] gives (curl u, x times p) = (curl Pi_m u, x times p). Membership of curl u in V^{Sf} instead requires (curl u, x times p) = (Pi_m curl u, x times p) on the reduced face DoFs [3]. The L^2 projection does not commute with differentiation (e.g. on [0,1], (Pi_1 x^3)' = 9/10 while Pi_0(3x^2) = 1), so the two constraints differ in general. The same mismatch arises for grad I^{Sn} against the reduced edge DoF [5]. Hence identities [2] and [3], and the inclusions grad V^{Sn} in V^{Se} and curl V^{Se} in V^{Sf}, are unproven and generally false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose reduced-DoF constraints that are compatible across the sequence (e.g. via projections commuting with grad/curl). It must then prove the commuting identities including the reduced DoFs.
issues.overall_effect: The serendipity exact sequence fails, and with it the curl estimate [2] of thmve, the node gradient estimate, and the claim that Pi_l can act on grad/curl of serendipity functions.
issues.title: Commuting diagrams/exact sequence for serendipity interpolants not established
issues.why_classification: The exact-sequence property is a central advertised feature. Restoring it requires redesigning the reduction constraints, which is new architecture rather than a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: For v in H^s we have grad v in H^{s-1}, so applying thmve to grad v yields at most h^{s-1}|grad v|_{s-1}. The stated seminorm |grad v|_{s,K} is undefined for v in H^s. Counterexample: at s=m+1 with v in P_{m+1}, the right-hand side vanishes. That would force grad(v - I^{Sn}v)=0, impossible because serendipity node functions are of degree m on edges.

issues.overall_effect: The stated H^1-seminorm rate is false; only the rate h^{s-1}|v|_{s,K} is supported, subject to the other issues.

issues.failure_explanation: thmve is stated only for edge spaces whose order equals [s], with beta=(m,beta_d,m-1). The edge space containing grad V^{Sn} has beta=(m-1,k_f,-1), and grad v lies in H^{s-1}. So thmve applies only when [s-1]=m-1 and m-2=-1. For most of the claimed range 3/2<s<=m+1 and m>=2, the cited result is not available. Moreover, under m=[s], thmve's own r-range (1/2,m] is empty for 1/2<s<1.

issues.failure_explanation: The functions psi_i^l lie in V^S_l, which is a subspace of V_l, and both change with l. No limit function psi_i^infty in L^2 is constructed, so the density-of-polynomials step has nothing to act on. Convergence of the norms ||Pi_l psi_i^l|| does not imply that the infinite rows (M_ij)_j are linearly independent. Linear independence of the psi^l for each l does not exclude a combination lying in ker Pi_l for every l. Hence the existence of an l with M^l of full row rank is a non sequitur. Even if granted, finite-dimensional norm equivalence gives constants depending on K and l (and l may depend on K). A uniform-in-l bound ||psi_i^l|| <= C_K is unsupported by fixed-degree estimates. Uniformity over meshes satisfying assmesh, needed for a stabilization-free scheme, is never addressed.
